rule: Experimental rearing, feeding, vaccination, growth, welfare, production-oriented physiology or husbandry work on an eligible species is relevant even without the word commercial, unless there is affirmative evidence that rearing is solely for release/restocking/stock enhancement, or the eligible salmonid is incidental.
refined_boundary: Basic laboratory physiology/toxicology/pathology does not become eligible merely because an eligible species is used; there should be a production-oriented rearing, feeding, vaccination, growth, acclimation or husbandry connection.

accepted.basis: Rainbow trout fry vaccine candidate; production-health intervention.
Atlantic salmon smoltification cage designed for holding and transport; husbandry method.
Rainbow trout dietary composition experiment with commercial diet and growth response.
Coho salmon seawater acclimation following transfer to seawater net pens; production-oriented smolt transfer physiology.
Pink salmon pen-rearing and growth experiment in a floating net pen.
Rainbow trout salinity adaptation with growth, mortality and ionoregulation measured in sea cages.
Seawater-acclimated rainbow trout feeding/digestion study using a commercial diet.
Hatchery-reared rainbow trout feeding physiology using commercial pellets; no affirmative release/restocking evidence.
Masu salmon juveniles are explicitly described as released from fish farms; affirmative hatchery-release context overrides rearing evidence.
Hatchery-scale whirling-disease filtration study is tied to Sport Fish Restoration, indicating stocking/release rather than commercial aquaculture.

held_for_other_rule.reason: Controlled co-infection/pathology study; production-health relevance is plausible but not a husbandry intervention.
Experimental disease transmission; net pens/ponds appear as inferred transmission settings rather than the actual production context.
